mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI increases do not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE rises significantly, or the correlation between UNRATE and S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals a weakening demand in the real estate sector, which often leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the instances where HOUST declines significantly, or the correlation between HOUST and S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increases significantly, or the correlation between INDPRO and S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS decreases, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS and S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS increases significantly, or the correlation between RSAFS and S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 0.5% MoM and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where both PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases significantly, or the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE on S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) coupled with an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases > 0.5% MoM and UNRATE increases > 0.3pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where both INDPRO decreases and UNRATE increases significantly, or the joint effect of INDPRO and UNRATE on S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
